newsitem.title: USA: Mercury Finance faces another lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Mercury Finance faces another lawsuit.

text.p: Another lawsuit has been filed against Mercury Finance Co, accusing the company of issuing false and misleading financial statements, according to lawyers for the plaintiffs.

The class action suit was filed in Chicago district court on behalf of buyers of the company's common stock between Jan. 30, 1994, and Jan. 28, 1997, said the law firm of Savett Frutkin Podell & Ryan, one of several law firms representing the plaintiffs.

On Jan 30, a lawsuit was filed in Chicago charging that the company violated securities laws after the auto-loan company said phony bookkeeping entries had inflated its earnings and that it fired its chief accountant.

The new complaint alleges that Mercury, its auditors KPMG Peat Marwick LLP and two of Mercury's senior officers, John Brincat and John Doyle, issued false and misleading financial statements that materially overstated Mercury's revenues and profits, which artificially inflated the price of Mercury's common stock throughout the Class Period.
